title: An infinite family of counterexamples to a question of Camina
summary: A.R. Camina and R.D. Camina posed in [CC06] the following question: Suppose there are two finite groups, one nilpotent and the other non-nilpotent, and the two groups share identical sets of conjugacy class sizes; must the non-nilpotent group possess a non-trivial center? Recently, W. Zhou [Zho25] gave a negative answer via a subtle and elegant construction of concrete counterexamples. Nevertheless, his approach relies on the existence of Sophie Germain primes, and thus fails to yield infinitely many counterexamples unconditionally.
